utterances.speaker: MR. RINDI
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, did you have a chance to go through your statement yesterday during the proofing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RINDI
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm going to ask you a few questions in this regard. Can I ask you in the first place about your religious background, briefly? What religion were your parents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My parents were of the Islamic faith, and I'm an atheist.

utterances.speaker: MR. RINDI
utterances.text: Thank you. And what religion were you brought up as?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Islamic Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. RINDI
utterances.text: Thank you. Usher, could you display now page 10 of the B/C/S version of the document on the screen. This is page 6 of the English version. Thank you. Witness, could you please look at the last paragraph of this page. This is paragraph 5 of the English version. I will now read it out to you: "I know that Seselj spent a night in Zvornik some 15 to 30 days before the war. He slept in Bosko Ceranic's house. Bosko's house was located in the town centre. I am not sure, but I think the name of the street is Brace Stefanovica. Bosko Ceranic was a manager of a furniture shop in Zvornik next to his house. The name of the shop was "Braca Jerkovic." Bosko always said that he did not belong to any party, but all the political meetings were held in his house. Bosko was about 50 years old and married with two sons and one daughter. The daughter was a judge, and one of his sons was working together with him in the shop." Witness, do you have any clarification to make in this regard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do. When I first came to Zvornik, I went to Bosko Ceranic's, because he's my friend, to tell him that I am angry at him because he did not help me get out of Zvornik. I believed the rumours that he was truly powerful and that Mr. Seselj had slept at his house. However, he dissuaded me as he spoke in all sincerity saying that he never asked anyone about anything and that what I heard were mere Zvornik rumours. So this statement is based on rumour rather than fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. RINDI
utterances.text: Thank you. Usher, could we now look at page 11 of the B/C/S version of the document, please. This still is page 6 of the English version. Witness, could you now please look at the last sentence of the first paragraph. This is the last sentence of the second-last paragraph in the English version. I will now read out this sentence for you. "Zuco's Yellow Ants were one of Seselj's units too." Do you have any clarification in this regard, Witness, with regards to this sentence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zuco's Yellow Wasps. Well, for a while people were saying "Ants." It was the Yellow Wasps, and they were the most elite unit, and Zuco was the commander. His brother, Dusan, who was called "Repic," was right by him. He committed quite a few crimes. I personally saw Zuco at the medical centre, where I was for a while -- where I was detained, rather, well, for about ten days. That's when he came. He bragged that he used to be a captain at the federal Ministry of the Interior and now he was leading an elite unit, that they were Seselj's men. Well, that would be about it. He wore a cap. He had a bit of a complex in terms of his personality. He had two pistols, one on either side, and he kept coming to reconnoiter on the positions facing town, where the defenders of Zvornik were, things like that. I was detained three times. The last one that you put to me and that we are together putting before the Court was the third detention. There were two before that for a day or two respectively. Once, I was interrogated by him in his room and asked how many defenders there were at Kula Grad. He proposed to me that I attend negotiations, to have a surrender of weapons, that nothing would happen to anyone. I said to him that I did not belong to that party, that I had no influence whatsoever, and then he gave up. I mean, I know him personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. RINDI
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, with the corrections that you just specified, does this -- does the statement accurately reflect the events that you described therein?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's rather sparse, but it does reflect the events.

utterances.speaker: MR. RINDI
utterances.text: Thank you. So if you were asked questions about those events today, would you give the same answers that are contained in this statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Unfortunately, my knowledge and my views were fully confirmed. The answers would be the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. RINDI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RINDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time I would like to move for the admission of 65 ter number 5040 under seal, which is the B/C/S version, and 5040A, which is the English version. So I would like to request admission under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, can we have an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter number 5040 will be Exhibit number P521, and the English translation will be attached to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RINDI
utterances.text: Thank you. I have just one more question for the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I do apologise, Mr. Rindi. And it will be admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. RINDI
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RINDI
utterances.text: Witness, in your statement, you mentioned that you heard from people of the existence of a number of mass graves in the Zvornik area. Has the existence of such mass graves been subsequently confirmed to you in any way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, confirmed fully, except for one. Due to the inaccessibility of the terrain, it hasn't been discovered yet. The others have been discovered, and unfortunately, I thought they were smaller. But in actual fact, they are much bigger than what people were telling me about before that. All the mass graves that I talked about have been confirmed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RINDI
utterances.text: Thank you. And which is the mass grave which has not been confirmed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a mass grave that is called "Sahmanske Stijene." I presented it graphically. That grave is on the road between Zvornik and Sarajevo, or rather, between Zvornik and Drinjaca, about 400 or 500 metres to the south of Divic. In Mali Zvornik, on the other side of the lake, again, 100 or 200 metres away, there is this locality called Sahar. This is the Muslim part of the settlement where refugees lived. Persons who were killed from the area of Cerska, Konjevic Polje, and Kamenica when there was this offensive against Serbians in 1993, were buried there at that locality. The burial took place by way of helicopters with nets because it was inaccessible just before Morillon came to Cerska, which is when he stated he did not see any traces of killings because the army made sure that they would collect all the corpses in nets and then transport them by helicopter to these caves. That proved to be correct further. The locals at Sahir, the people who told me about this, could not live for a year from the stench that was coming from there and the birds that were flying above these rocks all the time. So that's the only grave that hasn't been discovered yet, but it is assumed that that is the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. RINDI
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honours, this concludes my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, we have a few minutes left, and Mr. Seselj will not put any questions to you because he has told us that he would not put any questions to the witness when this Rule is applied. I would like to discuss the presence of the paramilitary formations in Zvornik amongst other Seselj's men you may have mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What can you tell us in accurate terms without bearing in mind rumours or hearsay? What did you actually see with your own eyes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had direct meetings with their commander, Zuco. That was his nickname. Later on, I found out what his exact name was, Repic -- and his brother Repic, rather. As a matter of fact, once he stopped me, checked my ID. However, since I was in the company of a Serb doctor, after a bit of bickering he let me go after all. I, personally -- I, personally, have not seen a single killing committed by Seselj's men. However, what happened in the Zvornik camps - there were a few at Karakaj; that's what I talked about to people -- actually, all these killings were committed by these formations. Later on, it turned out that these formations became even more powerful, that they did not obey orders from Serbia. However, they really were so powerful that no one could do a thing about them, even the official authorities whose commander was Marko Pavlovic, or rather, Branko Popovic. I also heard that that unit, sometime in July/August, that is to say, when they committed all these crimes, they were then disbanded, arrested by special units from Pale because the official authorities of Republika Srpska could not function because of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The first point, you say that you met their commander, Zuco, and you also met his brother, Repic. What entitles you to say that these two individuals were members of the Serbian Radical Party or were connected in one way or another with Mr. Seselj? Did they tell you that themselves, or is this something you inferred?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: While I was at the medical centre for about ten days, I was often at the director's office. On one occasion, Zuco barged into that office, and when he was speaking about what he represented, that he said he was actually the commander of the defence in Zvornik, and he said that he belonged to the special units of Mr. Seselj, Seselj's men. He, himself, said that in front of Dr. Jelkic, Muhamed Jelkic, who was director of that medical centre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you said that there were several paramilitary units in Zvornik, and you said something a while ago, which I'm hearing for the first time. You said that these units were disbanded because Republika Srpska in Pale sent special units to disband them. How do you know this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Upon arriving in Vienna where I was a refugee, (redacted) (redacted). Then I came across many refugees from Drina. I took statements from them and information, but at the same time I also read the entire Serbian press. In the meantime, I linked up with journalists from the Belgrade weekly "Vreme," Mr. Svarm, and Jovan Dulovic, and they gave me lots of information. I even have pictures of that unit lined up and disarmed. However, Mr. Dulovic also told me that immediately after they had been disarmed and after they had had their pictures taken, those who had disarmed them went to a big restaurant near Mali Zvornik, and they got dead drunk together with them. So the picture was just taken for the sake of the public.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you're saying that the units that disarmed these individuals did, in fact, disarm them, but none of this was true because they went and had a drink together in a bar afterwards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The name of the restaurant or cafe is a bit vulgar. It's called "The Four Tits."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "The Four Tits." Right. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: Registrar, please prepare an order for this to be redacted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: I made an effort for these observations not to come from only one side but from the other side too. I wanted to be as objective as possible. I had Serb friends, too, and I asked them about their views too. I think the book is a very valuable document in terms of what happened in Zvornik and around Zvornik during those four or five months.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Questions? Witness, it is now time to stop. I asked my colleague if he had any questions, and he said he didn't. On behalf of the Bench, I would like to thank you for having come to testify as part of the 92 ter proceeding, and I wish you a safe journey home. Madam Usher will escort you out of the courtroom in a few minutes. We shall start our hearing at 8.30 tomorrow morning, and we shall have a viva voce witness tomorrow. Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a procedural matter to deal with, but I'm going to wait for the witness to leave. I hope you have a minute for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one minute because I'm sitting in another case this afternoon and I need to prepare myself for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judges, today you admitted this statement according to Rule 92 ter. Up to page 7, the witness contains [as interpreted] what happened to the witness. After page 7, everything is hearsay. This is an unheard-of scandal when the witness himself gives up on part of the statement, when he claims that before the war for 15 or 20 days I slept in the house of a man in Zvornik. This is the first time that the witness told you personally that he saw Zuco and that Zuco told him that he was a man of Seselj's. It's not contained in the statement. And on the 9th of January, 1993, this statement -- this witness gave a statement to the Muslim authorities, and he identified Zuco as "Arkan's man." The OTP revealed this to me, so this is one scandal after the other. I'm just trying to tell you what it is that you come across when you take for granted these 92 ter statements. I'm not going to put any questions in this regard in the future, either, but I really wanted this objection of mine to be on the record as additional proof of why I'm against the application of 92 ter in these proceedings. Also, he says here that different groups of Seselj's men met and clashed. That is scandalous.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Seselj, I'm sure you have noticed that I put questions to him about this matter precisely, what entitled him to say that Zuco was one of Seselj's men, so I don't take things at face value, and I don't take what is written at face value. I ask questions. Your comment is therefore on the transcript. The Court stands adjourned. We shall resume at 8.30 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 17th day of July, 2008, at 8.30 a.m.
